slides.title: Every Lead Has a History.
slides.subtitle: Cora Recap Engine  ·  an operational AI system
slides.caption: An admissions team's calling system decides, lead by lead, when to call, text or email, and which campaign each lead belongs to.

slides.title: A status says where a lead stands.
slides.subtitle: Not how it got there, or what happens next.
slides.caption: The calls, the messages, the record of each campaign switch and the next scheduled job all sit in separate tables.
The first console joined them into one timeline in March 2026: calls, messages, and each campaign switch with its reason. It has since been replaced, and this copy runs on placeholder rows.
The current console reads the same records through three views. Lead Lifecycle gives one row per lead, with its first and current campaign and its next pending job.
Contact Drill-Down lays out six tables for one lead. None of them says why the lead's campaign changed.
The Pipeline Trace lists a lead's jobs in the order they run, but only the lead-level ones: for 200 sampled leads, 3,551 of 6,203.

rows: recorded campaign writes carry a reason
leads show their pending job as the next action
new leads carry a voice agent's line
slides.caption: Read from the system's own tables: only switches made from a call carry a reason, both views agree on the next action, and no new lead carries an agent's line.

slides.title: Fix the record, not just the view.
slides.subtitle: 24 and 26 August 2026.
slides.caption: A stale next-action time was cleared on campaign entry, calls were filed under the right campaign, and new leads took the number called instead of the agent's line.

slides.title: Where the history stops.
slides.subtitle: No reason on the current console. No proof of delivery.
slides.caption: Entries into a campaign write no reason, the current console does not show one, and 0 of 21,408 stored messages record whether they arrived.
